article_title: Using Machine Learning to Identify the Most At-Risk Students in Physics Classes
citation: Jie Yang, Seth DeVore, Dona Hewagallage, Paul Miller, Qing X. Ryan, and John Stewart. (2020). Using Machine Learning to Identify the Most At-Risk Students in Physics Classes. https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13575
title: DFW accuracy and precision as performance metrics for unbalanced classification outcomes in physics grade prediction
description: The article proposes evaluating grade-prediction classifiers on DFW accuracy (the fraction of actual DFW cases correctly classified, called sensitivity or recall) and DFW precision (the fraction of DFW predictions that are correct, the positive predictive value), because overall accuracy is uninformative when the outcome is unbalanced. With 10–20% of students receiving a D, F, or W, "overall accuracy would not be a useful metric to characterize model performance in this case" since guessing all ABC yields 80–90% accuracy. The appropriate balance between accuracy and precision depends on the cost and risk of the intervention.
requirements: Requires choosing the DFW outcome as the positive class and constructing a confusion matrix on a held-out test dataset
constraints: The correct balance of DFW accuracy versus precision must be selected based on the cost and risk of the intended intervention, as the article states
target_learning_goals: early identification of students at risk of receiving a D, F, or withdrawing
examples: Sample 1 models were tuned so DFW accuracy and DFW precision were approximately equal before comparison across samples
key_sources: Jie Yang, Seth DeVore, Dona Hewagallage, Paul Miller, Qing X. Ryan, and John Stewart. (2020). Using Machine Learning to Identify the Most At-Risk Students in Physics Classes. https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13575

article_title: Sensemaking and Scientific Modeling: Intertwined processes analyzed in the context of physics problem solving
citation: Amogh Sirnoorkar, James T. Laverty, and Paul D. O. Bergeron (2023). Sensemaking and Scientific Modeling: Intertwined processes analyzed in the context of physics problem solving. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03939
title: DFDIF account of modeling: Denotative Function, Demonstration, and Inferential Function as three components of modeling through external representations
description: Adopted from Suarez, the DFDIF account defines modeling as an activity engaged in by a cognitive agent involving abstraction and simplification of a phenomenon in order to generate explanations or predictions. It comprises the Denotative Function (elements of the target system are specified by elements of the external representation, the transition from physical world to model world), Demonstration (elucidating internal dynamics between denoted elements, typically via mathematical relationships), and the Inferential Function (interpreting theoretical relationships back onto the target system). The article uses it to categorize students' problem-solving moves.
requirements: An initial construction of a qualitative mental model, subsequently expressed through external representations.
constraints: Mental models are incomplete as they do not possess all the requisite information to comprehend and explain a complex context.
target_learning_goals: generating explanations or predictions about a physical context
examples: The article illustrates the components with Galileo's geometrical representation of uniformly accelerated motion, and maps the ACME protocol's three stages onto them.
key_sources: Amogh Sirnoorkar, James T. Laverty, and Paul D. O. Bergeron (2023). Sensemaking and Scientific Modeling: Intertwined processes analyzed in the context of physics problem solving. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03939

article_title: Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic: Physics Teaching in India
citation: V. Madhurima, Ram Ramaswamy, Deepa Chari, Vandana Nanal, and Tanushri Saha-Dasgupta. (2021). Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic: Physics Teaching in India. To appear in AIP conference proceedings of Women in Physics: 7th IUPAP International conference on women in Physics. https://sites.google.com/view/dfot2020
title: Discussion Forum for Online Teaching (DFOT): pan-Indian peer forum with 14 panel discussions and an 893-response survey
description: DFOT was initiated in mid-2020 because there was no pan-India forum for pedagogical discussion; its purpose was "to help teachers share resources, discuss best practices" and offer peer-to-peer training. It ran regular panel discussions with experts from all fields, regions, and institution types — "A total of 14 panel discussions were held between August 2020 and April 2021" — plus an email and social-media survey in which "893 responses were collected between August and December 2020," with results published online.
requirements: Teachers and other participants need internet connectivity and devices to join the online panel discussions and survey
constraints: The article notes these online initiatives were "operating for a restricted group of interested student -teacher community"
target_learners: School and higher-education physics teachers across India
target_learning_goals: Effective online teaching, evaluation, instruction, and student support
examples: Panel discussions on administration and online evaluation; survey results on devices and disconnections published online
key_sources: V. Madhurima, Ram Ramaswamy, Deepa Chari, Vandana Nanal, and Tanushri Saha-Dasgupta. (2021). Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic: Physics Teaching in India. To appear in AIP conference proceedings of Women in Physics: 7th IUPAP International conference on women in Physics. https://sites.google.com/view/dfot2020

article_title: A New Freely-Downloadable Hands-on Density-Functional Theory Workbook Using a Freely-Downloadable Version of deMon2k
citation: Oozeer, N. B., Ponra, A., Etindele, A. J., & Casida, M. E. (2022). A New Freely-Downloadable Hands-on Density-Functional Theory Workbook Using a Freely-Downloadable Version of deMon2k. https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16027
title: Freely-downloadable hands-on DFT Workbook using a free Linux serial version of deMon2k
description: The Workbook is a free teaching resource for practical DFT instruction at the Masters or advanced undergraduate level, built on a freely downloadable Linux serial version of deMon2k so students can run a fully functional quantum chemistry program on their own computers. It is structured as lessons with exercises and answers, and is intended to complement formal coursework. The authors state it is "intended to be complementary to this and to fu rther instruction in quantum chemistry and density-functional theory (DFT) in particular."
requirements: A Linux machine (or VirtualBox with Ubuntu) on which the freely downloadable serial version of deMon2k can be installed and run
constraints: Not intended to replace existing courses and basic textbooks; the authors do not claim the software is better than other software
target_learners: first-year Masters students in chemistry with some introduction to quantum chemistry
target_learning_goals: practical hands-on quantum chemistry and density-functional theory computation skills
transitioning to research-level use of quantum chemistry programs
examples: Used as a beta-tested teaching tool by a third-year undergraduate (NBO) and by a PhD student (AP) in Cameroon
key_sources: Oozeer, N. B., Ponra, A., Etindele, A. J., & Casida, M. E. (2022). A New Freely-Downloadable Hands-on Density-Functional Theory Workbook Using a Freely-Downloadable Version of deMon2k. https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16027
